title: What It Really Means to Be a Gentleman
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack), April 4, 2026
summary: Martin argues that a true gentleman goes far deeper than politeness or good manners—the word has become reduced to these surface behaviors when historically it meant honor, integrity, and how a man carried himself when no one was watching. Drawing on Saint John Henry Newman's observation that a gentleman carefully avoids whatever causes disturbance in others and seeks to put everyone at ease and at home, Martin contends that the true measure of gentlemanness is not social standing but how one makes others feel. A genuine gentleman demonstrates character and integrity in all actions, treats all people with equal respect regardless of station, and makes everyone feel valued rather than inferior.
points: True gentlemanhood transcends manners to require the highest degree of integrity and character—choosing the hard right over the easy wrong despite hardship or personal cost.
A gentleman does not place himself on a pedestal but effortlessly makes everyone feel respected and at ease, whether they understand proper etiquette or not—this is where his true nobility shows.
Chivalrous behavior means standing up for those who cannot stand up for themselves and demonstrating character and integrity in all actions, not just when observed.

Saint John Henry Newman captured the essence: a true gentleman's great concern is making everyone at their ease and at home, carefully avoiding whatever causes discomfort in the minds of those around him.
A man who believes himself above others due to social standing or wealth is not a gentleman at all; he is a snob—true gentlemanhood is about how one treats the vulnerable and unknown.
quotes: The world still needs gentlemen, but few understand what that means anymore. There was a time when the word represented more than status. It stood for honor, integrity, and how a man carried himself when no one was watching.

At his core, a gentleman must demonstrate the highest degree of integrity and character. He must do the right thing, even when no one might see his actions. He must choose the hard right over the easy wrong, despite any hardship or challenges that may come from the right decision.
A gentleman does not place himself on a pedestal or make others feel inferior; far from it. Rather, a gentleman seeks to put others at ease in all situations.

A true gentleman carefully avoids whatever may cause a jar or a jolt in the minds of those with whom he is cast; all clashing of opinion, or collision of feeling, all restraint, or suspicion, or gloom, or resentment; his great concern being to make everyone at their ease and at home.

Yes, a gentleman should be polite and exercise good manners, but it's how he makes others feel that truly matters. He puts others at ease while demonstrating character and integrity in all of his actions.
A man who thinks he's above others due to social standing or wealth is not a gentleman at all; he's just a snob.” Archived from The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack) on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
